title: Result chains
hints: Most functions are one-liners: `Ok` fills `val`, `Fail` fills `err`, `IsOk` is `r.err == nil`. When the compiler can't infer `T` from the arguments, instantiate explicitly: `Fail[U](r.err)`.

`Map` and `Then` start the same way: `if r.err != nil { return Fail[U](r.err) }`. Then `Map` returns `Ok(f(r.val))`, and `Then` can return `Of(f(r.val))` — a call returning `(U, error)` can be passed straight into a function taking `(v U, err error)`.

`Try` needs a named result and a deferred closure: `defer func() { if p := recover(); p != nil { r = Fail[T](fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrPanic, p)) } }()`, then `return Ok(f())`. `Collect` ranges with a counter `i`; on the first error `return nil, fmt.Errorf("item %d: %w", i, err)` — returning from inside the loop makes `yield` return false, so the source stops.
